extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, government officials, and scientific administrators designing federal medical research funding (e.g., agency creators, university leaders, foundation executives)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for establishing and administering a federal agency (National Foundation for Medical Research) and for supplying federal funds to support medical research, including types of support, governance, principles of administration, and priorities for institutions and investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrestricted grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds should be made available as unrestricted grants, with no portion earmarked for a specific purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unrestricted grants should supply technical help and materials; enable a limited number of young people to obtain research experience during their regular medical course; build up research in institutions where, for financial reasons, it is not now well-developed; and cover a multitude of research requirements within each institution. Administration of these funds should be decentralized to the fullest possible extent to allow medical school faculties and administrators to exercise judgment. A central agency attempting to underwrite such a program item by item would be prohibitively costly, rigid, and unable to meet diverse, rapidly varying institutional needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds should be made available to support fellowships so that young people with aptitude for research may be selected, trained, and given an opportunity to carry on research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships are intended to provide research experience during medical training and to develop future investigators; they are a distinct and essential form of federal aid complementary to general grants and larger project grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants-in-aid for major projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds should be made available to support special projects of considerable magnitude and importance by grants-in-aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants-in-aid are targeted support for large-scale, high-priority projects that exceed routine institutional capacities and warrant specific, substantial backing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor long-term grants (up to 10 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency should receive funds by such means as to permit it to favor long term grants, up to 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enabling multi-year support allows continuity for substantive research programs and is a design goal for federal funding mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate funding modestly and avoid excess
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal aid should be initiated modestly; funds exceeding the capacity of the Nation’s research institutions to utilize them effectively would do harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive early funding can encourage mediocre work and drive away university and foundation support. The Committee estimated approximately $5 to $7 million annually could be used effectively in the immediate postwar period, with growth only as institutional capacity and need develop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralized administration and institutional autonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Administration of funds should be decentralized to the fullest possible extent, allowing full play to the wisdom and experience of medical school faculties and administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decentralization preserves institutional flexibility and responsiveness; centralized, item-by-item underwriting would be administratively costly and too rigid to meet diverse and rapidly varying needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency independence from political influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible agency must remain free from political influence and resistant to special pressures; its policies must be determined by scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative autonomy should be structured to insulate funding decisions from politics and special-interest pressures; appointment and governance arrangements should reflect this need for independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to modify procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must have the necessary flexibility to modify its procedures in the light of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural adaptability is necessary to respond to evolving research needs and to improve operations based on experience; authority to modify procedures should be explicit in agency design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of trustees composition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The board of trustees would consist of five eminent scientists appointed by the President with the approval of the Senate for terms of 5 years, arranged initially to secure rotation by retirement of one member each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trustees would serve part-time, be paid for their work, be appointed without regard to civil-service laws, meet monthly (with one meeting annually in each of six geographical regions), determine the policies of the Foundation, and act on all requests for funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical board composition and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical board would consist of 12 scientists representing special fields of medical science, appointed by the trustees for terms of 3 years with rotation of 4 members each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical board members would serve part-time, be paid, be appointed without civil-service constraints, have necessary aides and ad hoc committees, forward requests for funds to the trustees with recommendations, follow the progress of supported work, and prepare reports or appraisals requested by the trustees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive secretary for business affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial and other business affairs of the Foundation would be in charge of a full-time executive secretary responsible to the trustees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full-time executive officer is required to manage the Foundation’s day-to-day financial and administrative operations under trustee oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation function: initiate and coordinate (not conduct) research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation would not engage in research but would initiate and coordinate research in existing institutions and maintain liaison with interested domestic and foreign agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation’s role is to stimulate, fund, coordinate, and liaise rather than to operate laboratories; it should leverage existing university and institutional capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for less-developed medical schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal aid should stimulate research in less favored schools to improve research facilities and staffs before considering establishing new institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeting weaker medical schools raises national research capacity; funds can develop research where financial constraints or lack of personnel currently limit contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance coordinated disease-focused and fundamental research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should include both coordinated attacks on particular diseases and independent studies of fundamental biological mechanisms; discovery cannot be achieved by directive alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee emphasizes that fundamental, curiosity-driven research is essential because many major discoveries (e.g., penicillin) arose from incidental observations in unrelated fields; funding policy should therefore support impartial development of a broad base of basic sciences alongside targeted programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities as primary locus for medical research and training
rubrics_metrics.description: The universities and medical schools are the chief contributors to pure science and are uniquely positioned to train investigators and integrate clinical and preclinical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal funding policy should strengthen university research and training, preserve academic freedom, and recognize the special duty of universities to provide untrammeled opportunities for imaginative scientific work; teaching hospitals, closely tied to schools, are also central to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and appraisal responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical board and Foundation should prepare reports or appraisals and the Foundation should produce reports as part of its functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reporting and appraisal of supported work and of Foundation policies are required to monitor progress, inform trustees, and guide future modifications of procedures.
